title: HttpTransport
description: The built-in HTTP transport's start options, in each role, and the HTTP client options the drive role and the broker descriptor share (spec.md §5.6, ADR 0035). The transport interface leaves a transport's options to the transport; these are the built-in one's.

ServeOptions.title: HttpServeOptions
ServeOptions.description: Where a served mock listens. Port 0 lets the system choose; the endpoint descriptor says which it chose.

DriveOptions.title: HttpDriveOptions
DriveOptions.description: Where a driven instance sends, what it adds to every request, and how it connects. Options the instance cannot act on fail transport/start with 'invalid-config' naming the member, so a run with a misconfigured provider fails before anything is sent.

base-url.description: An http or https URL. Its path prefixes every request's path: today's verifier's base path.

headers.description: Header name to value, added to every request and replacing a header of the same name, in any case, that the interaction carries: today's verifier's --header. Applied as the request is sent, after 'before-request' hooks. Values are never repeated in a log.

ClientOptions.title: HttpClientOptions
ClientOptions.description: How a client connects: the 'client' member of the HTTP transport's drive options and of the engine protocol's broker descriptor, so one configuration means the same thing to a provider and a broker. Every member is optional; a member the client does not know is ignored.

request-ms.description: How long a whole request may take, answer included. Default: 5000 for a provider (today's verifier's), 60000 for a broker. A transport/send that carries a shorter timeout-ms is bounded by that.

connect-ms.description: How long connecting may take, the TLS handshake included. Default: bounded only by request-ms.

http-version.description: '1.1' speaks HTTP/1.1 only (the default, today's verifier's); '2' speaks HTTP/2 only, by ALPN over TLS and with prior knowledge in the clear; 'negotiate' offers both by ALPN over TLS and speaks HTTP/1.1 in the clear.

retries.description: How many times a client that retries tries a request again. The broker client does (default 2: a request with no answer, a 5xx, or a 429 that says when), and so does an http hook (default 2 at the state points, 0 elsewhere: a 5xx, a 408 or a 429). A provider request is never retried: a verification observes the provider's first answer.

TlsOptions.title: HttpTlsOptions
TlsOptions.description: Which servers to trust, and how to prove who the client is. Certificates and keys are PEM text, never paths: a host reads the files.

ca-certificates.description: PEM text, each possibly a bundle, trusted beside the platform's roots rather than instead of them.

client-certificate.title: HttpClientCertificate
client-certificate.description: Presented when a server asks for one. 'certificate' may be a chain, leaf first. 'key' is a credential: never repeated in an event, an error or a log.

insecure.description: Accept any server certificate: today's verifier's --disable-ssl-verification. Default false.

ProxyOptions.title: HttpProxyOptions
ProxyOptions.description: Where requests go on their way. Absent, or kind 'environment': HTTPS_PROXY, HTTP_PROXY, ALL_PROXY and NO_PROXY where the engine runs, as today's verifier and curl read them. 'none': straight to the server. 'url': through 'url', except to the hosts 'no-proxy' names.

url.description: For kind 'url': an http URL. User information in it is never repeated in a log.

no-proxy.description: For kind 'url': hosts, domains (a leading '.' matches subdomains), addresses and CIDR blocks reached directly, in NO_PROXY's syntax.
